1. Model tends to overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
2. Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of a new trend; add 3–8% to forecast for early period.
3. Model shows persistent bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast horizon; apply downward adjustment of 1–3% for days 15–25.
4. Model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves; if forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
5. Model underestimates prices during periods of low volatility; increase forecast by 2–5% if 3+ consecutive days show low price movement (±1% range).
6. Model overestimates prices in the final 3–5 days of forecast; apply downward correction of 3–7% for last 3–5 days if true outcome shows downward trend.
7. Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; if true outcome drops by >3% from prior day, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 days.
8. Model overestimates prices during high volatility periods; if true outcome shows >5% daily volatility, reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 3–5 days.
